body.author: operator
body.text: Runs completed so far (191 of the planned runs) executed in a Linux cloud container (Intel Xeon 2.1 GHz, 2 cores, Python 3.13, --jobs 2). The session's background time limit stopped the runner; the remaining runs resume from this ledger on the operator's machine. Budgets are in checker calls, so machine speed affects only runs that reach the 900 s cap. Observation: 11 random-arm runs on tiny problems (lincode.n7.k4, qec.cyclic.n5.k1, qec.cyclic.n6.k1) reached the 900 s cap because almost every proposal was a duplicate of an already-checked candidate, and duplicates do not count against the check budget. Their best values are unaffected (the family is saturated) and the fair_checks outcome is read from the first 200 checks, so the comparison is hardware-independent; only wall time is spent.
